how_it_wins:
Land one commander, let it tax every card that moves, then end the game one of two ways. Shabraz takes a +1/+1 counter and 1 life per card you draw. Brallin takes a +1/+1 counter and deals 1 damage to each opponent per card you discard. A loot pays both once; a seven-card wheel pays both seven times (stack 001: Windfall makes two 10/10s and takes every seat to 33).

THE WHEEL is the proved ending. Wheel of Fortune with Consecrated Sphinx and both commanders out draws you 49 cards, Shabraz ends 52/52, and the cleanup discard of 42 fires Brallin until all three opponents are at 0 (stack 009). Without Sphinx a wheel softens the table and stops there: 21 per seat under Torbran (stack 005), 30 per seat with Artist's Talent at level 3 and Magmakin Artillerist (stack 004).

TWENTY-ONE is the stated ending, and it is unproven. Shu Yun, Embercleave, Blade Historian, Boros Charm and Akroma's Will each give double strike, but no passing stack resolves combat with any of them. The one stack that did (006) used Fireshrieker, which is cut. By arithmetic a 10/10 double-striker deals 20, one short; Embercleave's +1/+1 or Knowledge Is Power closes the gap. Check the numbers at the table before you swing.

What has to be true on the turn you go. A commander has resolved and survived a turn cycle. The wheel or the double-strike piece is in hand with the mana to cast it. A shield is up: Flawless Maneuver and Deflecting Swat are free with a commander out, and Grand Abolisher stops spells on your turn. Until then, hold the wheel. Game 002's hand of wheels with one creature did nothing.

The board picks the commander. Shabraz flies and every draw engine feeds him. Brallin is red, so Torbran adds to his damage and never to Shabraz's.

What the table misreads: a loot deck and two 3/3s. One wheel later it faces two 10/10s with every seat down 7.
mulligan:
Keep a hand that casts a commander on time and does something while it waits. Your rule from game 002: at most one wheel, and at least one creature or one ramp piece. The goldfish mulligans on lands alone (two to five) and keeps its first seven in 79.6% of games. Of the hands it kept, 80.2% pass your rule, so one kept hand in five still needs your eye.

Lands. In 10,000 first sevens, 1,935 had one land or none, 2,962 had two, 2,832 three, 1,632 four and 639 five or more. Land drops hit on turn 4 in 79.4% of games and on turn 5 in 70.8%. Keep two lands only with a rock: Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, Azorius or Izzet Signet, Talisman of Creativity. Game 003 was mana-starved for a round. Sol Ring is what made game 001 fast.

Check red. It is the short colour: 30 land sources against a target of 36. On curve with rocks it is 0.882, against W 0.907 and U 0.957. Brallin needs one {R}. Torbran, Gratuitous Violence and Fiery Emancipation each need {R}{R}{R}. Shabraz needs {W}{U}.

Cards that make a keep: Sol Ring, a Signet, Rhystic Study, Mystic Remora, Kitsa, Faithless Looting, Stoneforge Mystic (she finds Lightning Greaves). Cheap card flow now pays a commander later.

Ship lands and wheels with no creature and no rock. A wheel does nothing until a commander is out: the goldfish holds a mean of 0.607 dead wheels in hand on turn 1 and 0.622 on turn 2. Do not keep for Blade Historian, Embercleave, Gratuitous Violence or Fiery Emancipation. None of them does anything without a commander.

Gemstone Caverns: if you are not the starting player, it can begin on the battlefield making any colour. It costs a card from your hand.

combo_lines.001:
It turns on timing. Windfall's discard and draw are one resolution, and nobody gets priority inside it. All fourteen triggers wait until Windfall is in the graveyard, then you order them. Brallin is still a 3/3 through every draw.

What it proves: one Brallin trigger per card you discard. The opponents' discards pay nothing. Seven discards are 7 to each seat; seven draws are seven counters and 7 life on Shabraz. A wheel's damage is your hand size, not the table's. Windfall draws everyone the largest hand discarded, so a short hand of yours still refills to the table's largest.

What it does not prove: anything about combat. Two 10/10s are 20 each with double strike, by arithmetic, and no stack on this list resolves the swing.

Library of Leng, Sticky Fingers and Treasure Map // Treasure Cove in the hand shown are cut. They were discarded and did nothing in the line.
combo_lines.004:
It turns on Artist's Talent's level 3 being a replacement applied to each damage event on its own. Brallin's seven triggers are seven events, 1 + 2 = 3 each. Magmakin Artillerist's single trigger for the batch is one event, 7 + 2 = 9. Each opponent takes 30, 40 to 10.

What it proves: a per-event bonus pays many small pings more than one large blast. The extra 2 is dealt by Brallin or Magmakin, never by the Talent.

What it does not prove: a kill. Each seat keeps 10, which needs a second wheel or a swing. Shabraz is not on this board, so the draw half is unpriced. Level 3 costs eight mana across the three levels, each gained as a sorcery, so the Talent is a two-turn setup.

Sticky Fingers, Treasure Map // Treasure Cove and Swiftfoot Boots in the hand shown are cut. None of them acts.
combo_lines.005:
It turns on Torbran adding 2 to each separate damage event from a red source. Brallin is red, and his seven triggers are seven events: 3 each, 21 to every opponent.

What it proves: Torbran turns a seven-card wheel into 21 per seat. The stack's own title says the rest: not a kill from 40.

What it does not prove: anything from the Spider-Man, New Champion on this board. It is cut. Its 9 to one opponent is not in v2.1.1, so read the 21 per seat and drop the 30. Combat was scoped out. Whether Torbran's +2 on Brallin's strikes counts toward 21 commander damage is still an open question. Torbran never adds to Shabraz, who is white and blue.

Swiftfoot Boots in the hand shown is cut and does nothing here.
combo_lines.007:
It turns on who orders the replacement effects. The damaged player orders them, not you. One Brallin ping under Torbran, Gratuitous Violence and Fiery Emancipation can be 8, 10, 12 or 18 per seat. Each opponent applies both multipliers before Torbran's +2 and takes 8.

What it proves: price the smallest result. With all three out, every ping is at least 8 to each seat. Assuming each opponent minimises, five discards are 40 per seat by arithmetic. The discard came from Kitsa's loot, so one loot pays Brallin a counter and pings the table. Every card on this board is in the 99.

What it does not prove: combat. Gratuitous Violence and Fiery Emancipation multiply commander combat damage by oracle text, and no stack resolves it. All the damage here is noncombat, so none of it counts toward 21.
combo_lines.008:
It turns on Lae'zel replacing each counter placement once per trigger. Every Brallin trigger puts two counters, and so does every Shabraz trigger.

What it proves: five discards and seven draws make Brallin 13/13 and Shabraz 17/17. The damage stays 5 per seat, because Lae'zel changes counters, not damage. Windfall draws everyone the largest hand discarded. Here that was an opponent's seven, so you drew seven off a hand of five.

What it does not prove: the swing. A 17/17 Shabraz with double strike is 34 to one seat by arithmetic, and no stack resolves it. Lae'zel is one card: 7.1% of opening sevens, drawn by turn six in 18.1% (deck-audit).

Silence in the hand shown is cut and does nothing here.
combo_lines.009:
It turns on Consecrated Sphinx turning the table's draws into yours. Wheel of Fortune makes each opponent draw seven. That is 21 Sphinx triggers and 42 cards, plus your own seven. Shabraz ends 52/52 and you gain 49.

Then it turns on cleanup. You hold 49 cards, so cleanup discards 42 and fires Brallin 42 times. Triggers in cleanup open a priority window. After the 40th, all three opponents are at 0 and lose at once. No combat, and no mana after the Wheel.

What it proves: the one checker-passed table kill on the current 99. The Island on the board is not in the deck. It only paid mana.

What it does not prove: that the table lets it happen. Sphinx costs six and has to survive a turn cycle in front of everyone. Brallin is the half that kills; Shabraz's 52/52 is surplus. Your library needs 49 cards to draw. Grand Abolisher stops spells on the Wheel turn. Forge's AI held Wheel of Fortune in its cast proof, so only paper games will test this line.
combo_lines.010:
It turns on Kitsa's power. The copy ability needs power 3 or more, and Kitsa is a 1/3. She needs two prowess triggers this turn: Arcane Signet earlier, then the Wheel itself. The copy resolves first (discard three, draw seven), then the original discards those seven and draws seven more.

What it proves: one cast, two wheels. Ten discards pay Brallin ten times, so 10 to each seat and a 13/13. Fourteen draws pay Shabraz fourteen times, so a 17/17 and 14 life. The second wheel discards a full hand, so a short starting hand still pays twice.

What it does not prove: a kill. Each seat keeps 30. The line costs the Wheel's {2}{R}, Kitsa's {2} and a noncreature spell cast earlier in the turn.

threat_assessment:
Three games are logged, none on v2.1.1. Every table read below is an assumption.

WHEN YOU STOP BEING IGNORED. On turns one to four the table sees a loot deck and two 3/3s. Four signals end that read.
- Counters on a commander. The goldfish reads a mean of 9.346 commander counters by turn six and 22.386 by turn eight, a ceiling since it has no removal.
- A wheel resolving with a commander out. Stack 001: every seat to 33 and two 10/10s.
- Consecrated Sphinx beside Brallin. That board is stack 009, the table kill. Assume it draws the next removal spell.
- Torbran or a level-3 Artist's Talent beside Brallin: 21 or 30 per seat off seven discards (stacks 005, 004).
WHAT TO DO. Put the loudest piece down last. Cast Sphinx when the wheel can follow next turn, or behind Grand Abolisher. Land a commander on a quiet turn behind Lightning Greaves.

COUNT THEIR MANA FIRST. Assumption: a blue seat with two open holds a counter, and four open holds removal. Match the shield to the threat.
- Flawless Maneuver: free with a commander out; indestructible only. Exile, bounce and -X/-X go through.
- Akroma's Will, both modes with a commander out: protection from each colour and indestructible. Colourless removal goes through.
- Deflecting Swat: free with a commander out; it gives a targeted spell or ability a new target.
- Loran's Escape; Robe of Stars ({1}{W} phases the carrier out); March of Swirling Mist.
- Negate, Stubborn Denial, Izzet Charm: noncreature spells only. Denial is a hard counter once you control a creature with 4 power.
- Grand Abolisher: no spells, and no artifact, creature or enchantment abilities, on your turn. Land and planeswalker abilities still work.

THE GREAVES TRAP. Shroud stops your own targeting too. On a commander in Lightning Greaves you cannot equip, attach Embercleave, take Shu Yun's double strike, cast Boros Charm on it, place Inti's counter or use the commanders' cross-grants. Move Greaves first (equip {0}), or win with untargeted cards: Blade Historian, Akroma's Will, Knowledge Is Power, Gratuitous Violence, Jeskai Ascendancy.

TWO TAXES. Each cast from the command zone costs {2} more for every earlier one. Brallin was removed twice in game 001. Command Beacon puts a commander in hand, so that cast pays no tax.

WHAT YOU CANNOT ANSWER. Nothing in the 99 exiles a graveyard (deck-audit). Incendiary Command is the one sweep. Prismari Command and Chaos Warp handle artifacts, and Get Lost and Chaos Warp handle enchantments.
matchups:
By shape, anchored to cards and the three logged games.

SWEEPER CONTROL. You are the beatdown, because the long game is theirs. Commit one commander and keep the other in the command zone as the rebuild. Flawless Maneuver, Boros Charm's indestructible mode and Akroma's Will beat a destroy wipe only. Against exile or bounce, hold Negate, Stubborn Denial or Izzet Charm, or phase out with March of Swirling Mist.

COUNTERSPELLS AND DRAW-GO (Steven, game 001). A symmetrical wheel refills their hand too. Prefer the one-sided refills: Tolarian Winds and Fateful Showdown discard and redraw only your hand, and Collective Defiance's wheel mode targets one player. Resolve the commander when the blue seat is tapped. On the kill turn, Grand Abolisher stops every spell they hold, and a counterspell cannot touch the commanders' triggers. Wheel a blue seat into seven fresh cards only under Sphinx (stack 009).

GO-WIDE TOKENS (Stuart's zombies, game 001). Brallin's pings hit players, not creatures. Your one sweep is Incendiary Command, 2 to each creature, yours included. Go over the board instead. Shabraz flies, and his {W/U} gives Brallin, a Human, flying. Brotherhood Regalia makes a commander unblockable. Shabraz gains 1 life per draw and Bard has reach and vigilance, so you can race. Hit the token seat first.

COMBO. Held answers lose value against combo, so spend them. Hold one of Negate, Stubborn Denial or Izzet Charm rather than tap out for an engine. Grand Abolisher protects your turn only. Swords to Plowshares exiles, and Teferi, Master of Time's -3 phases a creature out at instant speed. Your clock will not outrun them. The goldfish's median kill is turn 7, against one seat with no blockers, and it kills by turn six in 31.0%.

STAX. Race it. A spell tax hits Shu Yun, Jeskai Ascendancy and Artist's Talent, which all want several noncreature spells a turn, so recount the hand. Chaos Warp and Get Lost answer the piece; Prismari Command destroys an artifact. Lightning Greaves at equip {0} survives an equip tax that Embercleave's {3} does not.

GRAVEYARD DECKS. Nothing in the 99 exiles a graveyard. Wheel of Fortune, Windfall, Reforge the Soul and Jace's Archivist fill every yard. Loot instead: Faithless Looting, Frantic Search, Kitsa, Mary Read and Anne Bonny and Teferi, Master of Time fill only yours.

TWO SEATS IN ONE TURN. Each 21 removes one opponent and leaves two with shots at you. The wheel under Sphinx (stack 009) is the one proved line that removes all three.
